name: Grand-Place
description: The city’s central square, surrounded by ornate guild houses and the Gothic town hall.

name: Belgian Comic Strip Center
description: A museum of Belgian comics, from Tintin onwards, in an art nouveau former textile warehouse designed by Victor Horta.

name: Atomium
description: A 102-metre steel model of an iron crystal, built for the 1958 World’s Fair, with exhibitions and a view from the top sphere.

name: Coudenberg Palace
description: The underground remains of the old palace of the dukes of Brabant, which burned down in 1731, beneath Place Royale.

name: Bourse
description: The 19th-century former stock exchange in the centre, now home to a museum of Belgian beer.

name: Tir National memorial
places: Tir National memorial (Edith Cavell execution site)
description: A memorial ground on the site of the old national rifle range, where German forces shot Edith Cavell and resistance members in both world wars.

name: Royal Museums of Fine Arts
places: Royal Museums of Fine Arts of Belgium
description: Belgium’s main art museums, from Flemish old masters to the Magritte Museum, in connected buildings near Place Royale.
